EXPLANATION

The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=1, so P4(x)=f(1)+f′(1)(x−1)+f″(1)2!(x−1)2+f‴(1)3!(x−1)3+f(4)(1)4!(x−1)4.

So we need to work out f(1), f′(1), f″(1), f‴(1) and f(4)(1), as follows: f(x)=2x2=2x−2⟹f(1)=2f′(x)=−4x−3⟹f′(1)=−4f″(x)=12x−4⟹f″(1)=12f‴(x)=−48x−5⟹f‴(1)=−48f(4)(x)=240x−6⟹f(4)(1)=240

Therefore, P4(x) is given by P4(x)=2−4(x−1)+122!(x−1)2−483!(x−1)3+2404!(x−1)4=2−4(x−1)+6(x−1)2−8(x−1)3+10(x−1)4.
